newsitem.title: UK: Lanica Trust dives after statement.
newsitem.headline: Lanica Trust dives after statement.

text.p: Shares in Lanica Trust Plc plummeted on Thursday after the company said it was unaware of any reason for the huge rise in its shares since last October.

In a brief statement issued after last night's close of trading in London, Lanica made no reference to speculation that it would be the vehicle for retail group Littlewoods to gain a stock market listing.
It pointed out that rules applying to listed investment companies meant it could not invest more than 20 percent of its gross assets in any one investment.
The stock, which embarked on a dizzying advance at the end of last October to peak at 21.00 stg on January 6, some 13 times its 158p level on October 30, was down 312-1/2p at 12.37-1/2 by 1021 GMT.
"Following recent press speculation, Lanica announces that it is not aware of any reasons for the substantial increase in the price of its shares over recent months," the statement said.

Lanica said it had made investments and could continue to evaluate opportunities, but would continue to manage its investment portfolio in accordance with the listing rules applying to investment companies.
Lanica Trust shares have already dropped this month after Littlewoods denied rumours that it planned to reverse its retail business into the company to gain a stock market listing.
Previously known as New Guernsey Securities, the company changed its name to Lanica when entrepreneur Andrew Regan took control last year -- at a time when the stock was trading at just 203p.
Littlewoods said on January 7 it was discussing "the possibility of a very small fulfilment operation on the catalogue front" with Lanica, but declined further comment.
